title: The Conjuring
tagline: Hide and clap. Then come to dinner.
about: Paranormal investigators help a family terrorised by a dark presence in their Rhode Island farmhouse.

    StartersRhode Island clam cakesFried clam fritters with chopped clams in a light batterHow to make it1 tin chopped clams200g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 egg1 L vegetable oil, for frying1 lemon, cut into wedges4 tbsp tartare sauceDrain the clams, keeping the juice.Mix the flour, baking powder, egg and some of the clam juice, then fold in the clams.Spoon into oil at 180°C and fry until puffed and golden.Serve with lemon and tartare sauce.Hide and clap cornmeal johnnycakesCrisp edged cornmeal griddle cakes served with butterHow to make it200g fine cornmeal1 pinch fine salt300ml boiling water100ml milk60g butter, plus extra to serve4 tbsp maple syrupPour the boiling water over the cornmeal and salt and stir. Loosen with the milk.Cook spoonfuls in butter on a griddle until crisp at the edges.Serve with butter and maple syrup.MainsWarrens' New England fish bakeCod fillets under a buttery cracker and lemon crust, with boiled potatoesHow to make it4 cod fillets100g crackers, crushed80g butter, melted1 lemon, zested2 tbsp chopped parsley800g potatoes, boiled300g frozen peasLay the cod in a dish. Mix the crackers with melted butter, lemon zest and parsley and press on top.Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.Boil the potatoes until tender and cook the peas. Toss both with butter.Perron farmhouse Yankee pot roastDinner for a family of seven in 1971How to make itAs written, serves 4Beef chuck seared dark and braised for hours with onion, carrot, celery and red wine, carved thick with potatoes, the braising gravy spooned over.Heat the oven to 160°C.Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and sear hard on all sides in a heavy pot.Add 2 onions in wedges, 4 carrots and 2 celery sticks in chunks and 2 garlic cloves.Pour in 250ml red wine and 500ml beef stock, add thyme and 2 bay leaves, cover and braise for 3 hours.Add 800g halved potatoes for the last hour.Lift out the meat and veg, reduce the liquid by a third and season for gravy.SweetsHarrisville farmhouse apple crispCinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble toppingHow to make it6 apples, sliced1 tsp cinnamon60g caster sugar1 lemon, juiced100g cold butter, cubed80g plain flour80g rolled oats80g brown sugar300ml pouring creamToss the apples with cinnamon, sugar and lemon juice in a dish.Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar and scatter over.Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes.Serve with pouring cream.Music box raspberry jam drop shortbreadThe little music box that plays by itselfHow to make itAs written, serves 4Buttery vanilla shortbread rounds with a thumbprint of raspberry jam baked in the middle, dusted with icing sugar and kept in a tin.Beat 200g soft butter with 100g caster sugar and 1 tsp vanilla until pale.Mix in 250g plain flour and 50g cornflour to a soft dough.Roll into 20 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays and press a hollow in each with your thumb.Fill each with half a teaspoon of raspberry jam.Bake at 170°C for 15 to 18 minutes until pale golden at the edges, cool on the tray and dust with icing sugar.DrinksRhode Island coffee cabinetCoffee syrup blended with milk and ice creamHow to make it250ml strong brewed coffee150g caster sugar500ml full cream milk8 scoops of vanilla ice cream4 tbsp whipped cream50g dark chocolate, to grateSimmer the coffee with the sugar for 10 minutes until syrupy, then cool completely.Blend some of the syrup with the cold milk and ice cream until thick and smooth.Pour into chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and grate chocolate over each.
